newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai officials to meet on plunging stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: Thai officials to meet on plunging stock exchange.

text.p: Thai finance ministry, central bank and stock exchange officials will meet on Tuesday to discuss the battered stock market, Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda said.
He said that he expected the dumping of bank stocks, which drove the local bourse to over three-year-lows on Monday, to be only a short term action.

"Yesterday there was dumping of bank stocks but it is not clear yet what triggered the sales. I believe it will be short term and will not cause much damage because our Thai stock fundamentals remain good," he told reporters.
Bodi said heavy sales by foreign investors on Monday, amounting to several billion baht, were only a small portion of the total they had invested in the bourse.
Bodi also said the market was anticipating lower third quarter earnings. But he said he believed fourth quarter results might improve in line with some economic indicators.
The stock index came under reduced pressure on Tuesday as sales volumes fell. At 0442 GMT, the index was down 1.44 percent or 13.56 points to 931.07.
